uzo.purpose: Sets running text in the system's type roles: body, caption, kicker, inline code.

instead.kialo: A text that heads a section is a heading with a level, because a screen reader lists the levels as the table of contents and a bold paragraph is not in it; that is the titolo.
A reference inside running text is a link, because a reader follows it from the sentence; the ligilo inline takes the text's role and breaks with it.
A status in one to three words beside a thing is a badge, because a status is read at a glance and never by colour alone; that is the insigno.

boundary.kialo: Text with its own structure — lists, emphasis, links written as Markdown — is content with a renderer, because every mark in it asks for an Ero of its own: the markdovido, which builds it from the Eroj and lets nothing of the source run.

containers.name: page-section
containers.kialo: A section of a page is its heading and the text under it, because the text is what the heading announces.

with.kialo: A link stands inside the text where the thought needs it, because a reader follows it from the sentence; the ligilo inline takes the role of the text around it.
A badge stands inside the text next to the word it describes, because a status is read at a glance where the sentence names the thing (Nachlese 7 ② B-10: phrasing content).
Code inside a sentence is a teksto with kind code, because it is spoken as code in the line of the text; a paragraph never holds a paragraph.
